texts: The autumn equinox took place on day 0 of Year 1.
Every autumn equinox begins moth-season.
The East Row is a lantern-row on the Cliff Path.
The Middle Row is a lantern-row on the Cliff Path.
The Harbor Row is a lantern-row along the harbor wall.
The Harbor Station is a lantern-station on the Cliff Path near the harbor.
Coraline Ash arrived in Aelmere in the late summer of Year 1.
Coraline Ash arrived two days before the autumn equinox.
Coraline Ash came on a market boat from a village down the coast.
Old Vesh and Coraline Ash met at the harbor.
Old Vesh walked with Coraline Ash to the Watch.
In the late summer of Year 1, two days before the autumn equinox, the Council questioned Coraline Ash at the Watch.
The questioning lasted for one afternoon.
Old Vesh said that the village lacked an apprentice candidate from a Keeper family that year.
The Council accepted Coraline Ash as an apprentice by a vote.
The Council assigned the apprentice Coraline Ash to Pell.
Pell was nineteen years old.
In the late summer of Year 1, on the first night of her apprenticeship, Coraline Ash did not light a lantern.
Coraline Ash walked the Cliff Path with Pell from sundown to dawn.
Coraline Ash carried Pell's leather case.
Pell cleaned the glass of the lantern.
Pell trimmed the wick of the lantern.
Pell filled the reservoir of the lantern with mire-essence.
Pell lit the lantern.
Coraline Ash wrote the steps in a notebook.
In the late summer of Year 1, one day before the autumn equinox, the salt-bloom store at Cauldron Hall held ten weeks of winter supply.
Hesper reported to the Council that the previous new-moon harvest had been thin.
In the late summer of Year 1, one day before the autumn equinox, Meren Tallowhand walked to a station on the Cliff Path at sundown.
Meren Tallowhand lit the lantern at the station.
The lantern burned mire-essence.
The lantern produced mist-light.
The mist-light attracted nightmoths.
Meren Tallowhand counted seventeen nightmoths at the lantern at the third watch.
A handful of nightmoths gathered at the Middle Row that night.
All the sky-cats stayed on the cliff-spires that night.
In the late summer of Year 1, one day before the autumn equinox, Bevin Coombe walked the Cove Stair at sundown.
Bevin Coombe touched the iron bands of the Stilllight Lantern.
Bevin Coombe lit the Stilllight Lantern.
The Stilllight Lantern burned mire-essence from dusk until dawn.
Bevin Coombe walked the Cove Stair again at midnight.
Bevin Coombe walked the Cove Stair again at the third watch.
Bevin Coombe refreshed the mire-essence of the Stilllight Lantern at midnight.
Bevin Coombe trimmed the wick of the Stilllight Lantern at the third watch.
On day 0 of Year 1, the night of the autumn equinox was clear and mild.
Keepers counted about twenty-five nightmoths at each lantern of the Cliff Path.
A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the East Row.
Three sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.
The three sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the East Row.
The nightmoth crowd at the East Row shrank.
Keepers counted seven nightmoths at the East Row at the third watch.
Each nightmoth that survived the hunt fled to the Hollows.
On day 0 of Year 1, Coraline Ash carried Pell's leather case on the Cliff Path.
Coraline Ash and Pell watched the sky-cat hunt at the East Row from the Middle Row.
Pell told Coraline Ash that surviving nightmoths flee to the dim lanterns of the Hollows.
Coraline Ash wrote Pell's explanation in the notebook.
On day 1 of Year 1, Tessa Brae walked the base of the cliff in the morning.
Two assistants walked with Tessa Brae.
The three sky-cats had molted during the hunt.
Feathers had fallen to the base of the cliff.
Tessa Brae collected forty-one of the fallen feathers at the base of the cliff.
Tessa Brae weighed the feathers at the Watch.
Tessa Brae recorded the feathers in a ledger of the Watch.
Tessa Brae added the feathers to the feather bin.
On day 1 of Year 1, Pell collected silken threads from the lanterns of the Cliff Path at dawn.
Nightmoths had landed on the lanterns during the night.
The nightmoths had left silken threads on the lanterns.
Pell carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper filled the three cauldrons with sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in the sea-water.
Mire-essence formed in the three cauldrons by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in three clay vessels.
On day 3 of Year 1, Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row at sundown.
The lanterns burned mire-essence.
The lanterns produced mist-light.
The mist-light attracted nightmoths.
Many nightmoths gathered at the lanterns of the East Row.
The nightmoths landed on the lanterns.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns.
Pell collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 4 of Year 1.
Pell carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the second cauldron on day 4 of Year 1.
Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in two clay vessels.
Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row with the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 4 of Year 1.
On day 16 of Year 1, a cold wind blew off the sea at night.
The cold wind was a north wind.
The cold wind struck the Cliff Path at night.
The cold wind came before the first hard frost.
The salt-bloom season had not yet started.
The keepers on the Cliff Path had not yet added salt-bloom to the mire-essence of their lanterns.
That night, eleven lanterns on the Middle Row were unprepared.
The eleven lanterns went out before dawn.
No lantern at the Sunken Cove went out.
No lantern in the Northcove went out.
The cliff-spires sheltered the Northcove against the north wind.
On day 17 of Year 1, the Council held an emergency meeting in the afternoon.
The Council decided to begin salt-bloom additions that afternoon.
Hesper distributed pouches of salt-bloom to the keepers of the Cliff Path.
The Council spoke to the keepers of the Northcove.
The Northcove did not need salt-bloom.
The Council recorded the cold snap in the ledger.
On day 17 of Year 1, the keepers on the Cliff Path added salt-bloom to the mire-essence of their lanterns at sundown.
The mire-essence in the lanterns burned slowly.
The cold wind struck the Cliff Path again that night.
No lantern on the Cliff Path went out that night.
The cold snap ended after three nights.
The Council continued to distribute salt-bloom throughout the rest of the autumn.
On day 17 of Year 1, Keepers had relit the eleven lanterns of the Middle Row.
The eleven lanterns burned dimly.
The dim lanterns gave weak mist-light.
The weak mist-light attracted a handful of nightmoths.
Keepers counted twelve nightmoths at the Middle Row that night.
The thread harvest at the Middle Row fell.
Pell and Coraline Ash collected a handful of silken threads from the Middle Row the next morning.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water at Cauldron Hall that day.
The cauldrons yielded two vessels of mire-essence.
The cauldrons had yielded three vessels of mire-essence on day 1.
On day 17 of Year 1, Pell told Coraline Ash at midnight that a dim lantern gives weak mist-light.
Pell told Coraline Ash that weak mist-light attracts a handful of nightmoths.
Pell told Coraline Ash that a handful of nightmoths leaves a small heap of silken threads.
Coraline Ash wrote in the notebook that the lantern, the nightmoths, the silken threads and the mire-essence form a closed loop.
On day 21 of Year 1, the moon was full.
The Council convened at the Watch.
The Council redistributed mire-essence across the lantern-stations.
The Northcove stations contributed mire-essence to the central pool.
The Council issued mire-essence from the central pool to the stations of the Middle Row.
The Council recorded the redistribution in the Watch ledgers.
On day 21 of Year 1, Hesper reported to the Council that the cold snap had cost about one and a half vessels of mire-essence.
Hesper reported to the Council that the salt-bloom store held eight weeks of winter supply.
Brindle Coombe reported to the Council that the Northcove production was normal.
Sailsworn reported to the Council that the next new moon was twelve days away.
Sailsworn reported to the Council that twelve members would form the harvest party.
Old Vesh proposed that Coraline Ash join the salt-bloom harvest party.
The Council agreed that Coraline Ash would join the harvest party.
On day 33 of Year 1, a harvest party of twelve people left Aelmere at sundown.
Sailsworn led the harvest party along the goat-path to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
The harvest party carried copper buckets and wooden scrapers.
Coraline Ash walked with the harvest party.
Sailsworn assigned each member of the harvest party to one of the five blooming pools in the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
Sailsworn assigned Coraline Ash to the second pool from the north.
On day 33 of Year 1, Coraline Ash harvested salt-bloom at the new moon.
Coraline Ash scraped the submerged stones in the second pool with a wooden scraper.
Salt-bloom came off the stones in pale flakes.
Coraline Ash gathered the flakes with a fine net.
The harvest party rotated pools at midnight.
The harvest party rotated pools again at the third watch.
The harvest party inspected the two southern pools.
The two southern pools did not bloom that night.
The harvest ran from dusk until dawn.
On day 34 of Year 1, the harvest party returned to Cauldron Hall at dawn and carried twelve full buckets of salt-bloom.
The harvest was heavy.
Hesper poured the salt-bloom into the salt-bloom store.
Hesper wrote the date on each compartment of the store.
The salt-bloom stayed potent.
On day 47 of Year 1, the moon was full.
The Council convened at the Watch.
Sailsworn reported to the Council that the salt-bloom store held fourteen weeks of winter supply.
The Council issued the standard winter feather ration to the Stilllight Station.
Bevin Coombe reported to the Council that the Stilllight Lantern had remained free of wraiths.
Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the feather store held eight weeks of supply.
The Council issued an extra feather ration to the Stilllight Station.
The Council issued an extra feather ration to the stations of the West Row.
On day 60 of Year 1, about four sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires in the morning.
In a normal autumn about ten sky-cats are visible on the cliff-spires in the morning.
A handful of sky-cats had been visible on the cliff-spires for two weeks.
A handful of sky-cats had hunted on the Cliff Path in those two weeks.
A handful of sky-cats had molted in those two weeks.
Tessa Brae collected about twelve feathers per morning during those two weeks.
In a normal autumn Tessa Brae collects about thirty-five feathers per morning.
On day 68 of Year 1, the moon was full.
The Council convened at the Watch.
The Council discussed the sky-cat drought.
Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the autumn feather store would be small.
The Council discussed a stricter feather ration for the winter.
Old Vesh reported to the Council that a thin feather autumn had also come before the bad winter of twenty-six years ago.
The Council recorded the observation in the ledger.
On day 68 of Year 1, Pell told Coraline Ash that sky-cats molt while they hunt.
Pell told Coraline Ash that molting sky-cats drop feathers.
Coraline Ash wrote in the notebook that a thin sky-cat year brings a thin feather harvest.
Old Vesh told Pell that the village always keeps the Stilllight Lantern lit.
On day 75 of Year 1, a sky-cat hunted nightmoths at the Sunken Cove on a clear night.
Sky-cats rarely hunt at the Sunken Cove.
The Council discussed burning wintergloss at the Stilllight Lantern.
Wintergloss repels nightmoths from a lantern.
The Council declined the wintergloss, because the Stilllight Lantern drew a handful of nightmoths.
On day 80 of Year 1, the Council approved half-shifts for Coraline Ash at the Harbor Station.
A senior Keeper had retired from the Harbor Station, so the Harbor Station had been unstaffed.
Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown for the first time.
Pell stood beside Coraline Ash.
The wick caught cleanly.
The lantern burned mire-essence.
The lantern produced mist-light.
The mist-light attracted nightmoths.
A nightmoth landed on the lantern after sundown.
The nightmoth left silken threads on the lantern.
Pell joined Coraline Ash at the Harbor Station at midnight and at the third watch.
On day 85 of Year 1, the lanterns at the Hollows drew many nightmoths.
The lanterns of the Cliff Path drew a handful of nightmoths that autumn.
A handful of sky-cats hunted on the Cliff Path that autumn, so a handful of nightmoths fled to the Hollows.
Pell wrote a note about the Hollows for the Council.
The thread harvest at the Hollows rose in that week.
The thread harvest on the Cliff Path stayed thin in that week.
On day 92 of Year 1, the first hard frost came.
The harbor was white with rime in the morning.
The cold wind blew off the sea from dusk until dawn.
Every lantern on the Cliff Path held salt-bloom in its mire-essence.
The mire-essence burned slowly.
Every lantern on the Cliff Path stayed lit from dusk until dawn.
On day 96 of Year 1, the moon was full.
The Council convened at the Watch.
The Council opened the salt-bloom season.
The Council standardized the salt-bloom rations for the winter.
The Council exempted the Northcove from salt-bloom.
Hesper reported to the Council that the thread harvest was thin.
Cauldron Hall distilled at reduced volume during the frost weeks, because the thread harvest was thin.
Hesper said that the cold months would yield about eight vessels of mire-essence.
On day 96 of Year 1, Brindle Coombe said at the Council that the village was behind on mire-essence.
Brindle Coombe said at the Council that the village was behind on feathers.
Brindle Coombe said at the Council that a hard winter would force the village to dim some lanterns.
Old Vesh said at the Council that the village always keeps the Stilllight Lantern lit.
On day 100 of Year 1, Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown.
The lantern burned mire-essence.
The mire-essence in the lantern held salt-bloom.
The mire-essence burned slowly.
The lantern produced mist-light.
The mist-light attracted nightmoths.
The nightmoths landed on the lantern.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lantern.
Coraline Ash collected the silken threads from the lantern at dawn on day 101 of Year 1.
Coraline Ash carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the third cauldron on day 101 of Year 1.
Mire-essence formed in the third cauldron by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in a clay vessel.
Coraline Ash drew the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 101 of Year 1.
On day 111 of Year 1, Lantern-night fell.
Lantern-night is the longest night of the year.
The night was clear and very cold.
Every lantern in Aelmere was lit.
Meren Tallowhand lit the Stilllight Lantern at sundown as the speaker of the Council.
Every villager walked the Cliff Path at midnight from the harbor wall to the cliff-spires.
The cold wind blew strongly that night.
Every lantern on the Cliff Path held.
Coraline Ash walked beside Pell.
Joren Salt walked beside Meren Tallowhand.
The villagers told stories at the harbor fires until dawn.
Old Vesh told the story of the bad winter of sixty-three years ago.
Three sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires in the morning.
On the night of day 111 of Year 1, Bevin Coombe was ill.
Halden tended the Stilllight Lantern that night in place of Bevin Coombe.
Halden was a substitute Keeper.
Halden refilled the mire-essence of the Stilllight Lantern at midnight.
The wick of the Stilllight Lantern was carbonized.
Halden did not trim the wick.
The Stilllight Lantern burned dim for three hours.
The Stilllight Lantern gave weak mist-light for three hours.
The Council judged that the dim burning was equivalent to an untended night.
On day 120 of Year 1, a wraith emerged from the water of the Sunken Cove, because the Stilllight Lantern had burned dim on the night of day 111.
The Stilllight Lantern had burned dim nine days before the emergence.
Marra Tallowhand saw the wraith first from her station near the Cove Stair.
Marra Tallowhand walked to the Stilllight Lantern.
Bevin Coombe was already at the Stilllight Lantern.
Bevin Coombe ground feathers.
Bevin Coombe scattered the ground feathers around the Stilllight Lantern.
The ground feathers warded the Stilllight Lantern against the wraith.
The wraith approached the Stilllight Lantern.
The wraith turned away from the Stilllight Lantern.
The wraith did not drain the Stilllight Lantern.
On day 121 of Year 1, the wraith approached a lit lantern on the West Row.
The wraith drained mire-essence from the lantern.
The drained lantern gave weak mist-light for the rest of the night.
The weak mist-light attracted a handful of nightmoths.
The wraith persisted for eleven days.
The wraith drained six lanterns on the West Row during its persistence.
Keepers counted about six nightmoths at each drained lantern during the persistence.
The thread harvest at the West Row fell sharply during that week.
The West Row is a lantern-row on the Cliff Path near the Sunken Cove.
On day 123 of Year 1, the Council held an emergency session.
The stations of the West Row requested feather rations from the Council.
The Council doubled the feather rations of the West Row stations.
On day 128 of Year 1, the Council held a second emergency session.
The Council reprimanded Halden.
Bevin Coombe said to the Council that Halden was inexperienced.
The Council issued a written warning to Halden.
Halden remained eligible for a station.
On day 131 of Year 1, the wraith faded back into the water of the Sunken Cove in the morning.
Hesper refilled the mire-essence of the six drained lanterns during the following week.
The six lanterns returned to normal mist-light during the following week.
On day 131 of Year 1, a second cold snap came.
The cold wind was unusually sharp that night.
Three lanterns on the Cliff Path went out before dawn.
The three lanterns held salt-bloom in their mire-essence.
The three lanterns went out despite the salt-bloom.
The Council recorded the night as an extreme cold event.
Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the feather store held four weeks of supply.
The wraith response had used half of the autumn feather store.
On day 145 of Year 1, the moon was new.
A spring tide filled the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
Salt-bloom bloomed in the tide-pools.
The harvest party walked to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools at sundown.
Coraline Ash carried a copper bucket and a wooden scraper.
Coraline Ash harvested salt-bloom at the third pool from the north.
Coraline Ash filled the bucket by the third watch.
The harvest party returned to Cauldron Hall and carried eleven buckets of salt-bloom.
The salt-bloom store rose to ten weeks of winter supply.
On day 155 of Year 1, six sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires in the morning.
Tessa Brae collected about twenty feathers per morning in that week.
Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the sky-cats had begun to return.
Bevin Coombe asked the Council to consider Halden for a permanent station.
Halden had tended the Stilllight Lantern well since the wraith.
The Council approved an apprenticeship-completion track for Halden.
On day 190 of Year 1, Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown.
The lantern burned mire-essence.
The lantern produced mist-light.
The mist-light attracted a handful of nightmoths.
Coraline Ash counted four nightmoths at the lantern at the third watch.
The nightmoths landed on the lantern.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lantern.
Coraline Ash collected a small heap of silken threads from the lantern at dawn on day 191 of Year 1.
Coraline Ash carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the first cauldron on day 191 of Year 1.
Mire-essence formed in the first cauldron by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in a clay vessel.
Coraline Ash drew the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 191 of Year 1.
On day 210 of Year 1, the spring equinox came.
On day 216 of Year 1, the moon was full.
The Council closed the salt-bloom season at the full-moon meeting.
The Northcove resumed its usual production.
The stations of the Cliff Path stepped down salt-bloom additions during the following two weeks.
The thread harvests returned to spring levels.
Cauldron Hall began a heavier distillation cycle.
The feather store held three weeks of supply at the end of the winter.
About ten sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires in the morning by the spring equinox.
On day 230 of Year 1, Coraline Ash began a solo stretch of thirty nights at the Harbor Station.
Pell did not accompany Coraline Ash during the solo stretch.
Pell visited the Harbor Station on her own off-nights.
During the solo stretch, Coraline Ash lit the lantern at sundown every night.
During the solo stretch, Coraline Ash refreshed the mire-essence at midnight every night.
During the solo stretch, Coraline Ash trimmed the wick at the third watch every night.
During the solo stretch, Coraline Ash extinguished the lantern at dawn every night.
Coraline Ash kept the notebook carefully.
On day 246 of Year 1, a thin fog came in off the sea in the evening.
The fog reduced visibility on the Cliff Path.
Coraline Ash kept the lantern of the Harbor Station burning steadily.
The lantern produced mist-light through the fog.
The mist-light attracted nightmoths.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lantern.
Coraline Ash collected about thirty-five silken threads from the lantern the next morning.
On day 251 of Year 1, the cold wind returned briefly at night.
The lantern of the Harbor Station held salt-bloom in its mire-essence.
The cold wind struck the lantern.
The lantern stayed lit.
On day 258 of Year 1, a crowd of nightmoths gathered at the Harbor Row.
Three sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.
The three sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row.
The nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row shrank.
Coraline Ash counted twenty-four nightmoths at the lantern of the Harbor Station before the hunt.
Coraline Ash counted nine nightmoths at the lantern of the Harbor Station after the hunt.
Coraline Ash wrote notes about the hunt.
On day 259 of Year 1, Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown on the thirtieth night of the solo stretch.
Coraline Ash completed thirty solo nights.
Coraline Ash's solo count reached thirty.
Pell and Coraline Ash met at dawn on day 260 of Year 1.
Coraline Ash and Pell walked back to Aelmere together.
The Council met in an informal session on day 260 of Year 1.
The Council invested Coraline Ash as a Keeper.
Coraline Ash lit her first lantern as a Keeper at sundown.
Meren Tallowhand placed a hand on Coraline Ash's shoulder.
Meren Tallowhand repeated the phrase.
Every villager present repeated the phrase.
On day 270 of Year 1, the village held the summer feast at midsummer.
The keepers of Aelmere ate together at the village square at midday.
The Council toasted the investiture of Coraline Ash.
The Council toasted the investiture of Mira.
Mira had completed her apprenticeship at the summer solstice.
On day 270 of Year 1, Meren Tallowhand told Old Vesh that the year had been difficult.
The village lost three lanterns to cold snaps in Year 1.
The village lost no lantern to the wraith beyond the six drained lanterns.
The six drained lanterns recovered.
The feather store nearly ran out in the winter of Year 1.
Old Vesh told Meren Tallowhand that the sky-cat drought had caused the near-miss.
Old Vesh proposed that a few stations of the Cliff Path burn extra mire-essence in early winter in order to draw crowds of nightmoths.
Old Vesh proposed that the bright stations keep sky-cats hunting on the Cliff Path.
The Council took the proposal under consideration.
On day 300 of Year 1, the keepers of the Harbor Row lit the lanterns of the Harbor Row at sundown.
The lanterns burned mire-essence.
The lanterns produced mist-light.
The mist-light attracted nightmoths.
A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the Harbor Row.
Three sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.
The three sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row.
The nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row shrank.
Each nightmoth that survived the hunt fled to the Hollows.
The lanterns at the Hollows gained silken threads that night.
The three sky-cats molted during the hunt.
Feathers fell to the base of the cliff.
Nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns of the Harbor Row.
The keepers of the Harbor Row collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 301 of Year 1.
On day 301 of Year 1, the keepers of the Harbor Row carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the three cauldrons.
Mire-essence formed in the three cauldrons by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in four clay vessels.
The keepers of the Harbor Row drew the stored mire-essence at sundown.
Tessa Brae collected thirty of the fallen feathers at the base of the cliff in the morning.
Tessa Brae added the feathers to the feather bin.
Bevin Coombe took feathers from the feather bin.
Bevin Coombe ground the feathers.
Bevin Coombe scattered the ground feathers around the Stilllight Lantern at sundown.
The ground feathers warded the Stilllight Lantern against wraiths.
No wraith approached the Stilllight Lantern that night.
On day 365 of Year 2, the second autumn equinox came.
Year 2 began on day 365.
The feather store held eight weeks of supply.
About ten sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires in the morning.
The salt-bloom store held eleven weeks of winter supply.
The mire-essence store had not yet recovered from the losses of Year 1.
On day 365 of Year 2, Coraline Ash inherited the Harbor Station.
Coraline Ash wrote her own log every night.
Pell took an apprentice named Roben.
Roben came from a Keeper family.
Pell carried the role of senior Keeper with ease.
On day 365 of Year 2, the moon was full.
The Council convened at the Watch.
The Council accepted Old Vesh's bright-station proposal.
The Council issued extra mire-essence rations to three stations of the Middle Row in order to draw crowds of nightmoths.
The Council issued the extra rations in order to keep sky-cats hunting on the Cliff Path.
On day 380 of Year 2, Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown.
The lantern burned mire-essence.
The lantern produced mist-light.
The mist-light attracted nightmoths.
A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the Harbor Row.
Two sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.
The two sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row.
The nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row shrank.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lantern.
Coraline Ash collected the silken threads from the lantern at dawn on day 381 of Year 2.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the second cauldron on day 381 of Year 2.
Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in a clay vessel.
Coraline Ash drew the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 381 of Year 2.
On day 395 of Year 2, the first cold snap of Year 2 came.
Every lantern on the Cliff Path already held salt-bloom in its mire-essence.
No lantern went out.
The three bright stations burned extra mire-essence.
The three bright stations produced strong mist-light.
The strong mist-light attracted crowds of nightmoths.
Keepers counted about thirty nightmoths per night at each bright station.
A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the Middle Row on six of the next ten nights.
Sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires on those six nights.
The sky-cats hunted nightmoths at the Middle Row on those six nights.
The sky-cats molted during the hunts.
Feathers fell to the base of the cliff.
The feather harvest in the following month was strong.
On day 396 of Year 2, Coraline Ash wrote in her log that a bright lantern draws a crowd of nightmoths.
Coraline Ash wrote in her log that a crowd of nightmoths brings sky-cats down from the cliff-spires.
Coraline Ash wrote in her log that hunting sky-cats molt feathers.
Coraline Ash wrote in her log that ground feathers make the Sunken Cove safe.
Coraline Ash read the note to Pell at breakfast.
On day 410 of Year 2, a gust of wind extinguished a lantern on the Middle Row in the evening.
Marra Tallowhand saw the gust from her station.
Marra Tallowhand walked to the lantern.
Marra Tallowhand relit the lantern within the hour.
The lantern was not at the Sunken Cove.
No wraith emerged.
The Council recorded the incident as a minor weather event.
Marra Tallowhand recommended that the Council issue extra mire-essence to the wind-exposed lanterns of the Cliff Path.
The Council took the recommendation under advisement.
On day 425 of Year 2, Hesper proposed an experiment with three water sources.
The Council approved the experiment.
Hesper filled the first cauldron with sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
Hesper filled the second cauldron with sea-water from the deep ebb.
Hesper filled the third cauldron with harbor water from the middle of the pier.
Hesper boiled silken threads in the three cauldrons for one day.
Mire-essence formed in the first cauldron.
The first cauldron yielded one vessel of mire-essence.
Mire-essence formed in the second cauldron.
The second cauldron yielded one vessel of mire-essence.
No mire-essence formed in the third cauldron.

Tam Harrow trimmed the wick.

Cauldron Hall increased its distillation.
Hesper assigned an extra apprentice to the morning collection of silken threads.
